clue.text: In the distance, an expedition in Africa without any clothes

indicators.note: the word is stripped of its clothes, its outer letters at each end

parts.note: a safari is an expedition, typically in Africa, to watch or hunt animals

explanation.surface: Far off, a group on an African expedition is going naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without any clothes' strips the outer S and I off SAFARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at or to a great distance, so it means far away.

clue.text: Strict believers give money — truly and surprisingly, it lasts

parts.note: to fund something is to give money to it
amen means so be it, truly

indicators.note: the words are arranged surprisingly, in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: Devout believers donate cash, and astonishingly their faith endures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'truly' gives the word said at the end of a prayer, and 'surprisingly' rearranges the last two words of the clue to finish the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentalists hold to the strict, literal interpretation of their religious texts.

clue.text: Better retool, if it helps keep you dry

indicators.note: to better something is to rework it into an improved shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to upgrade your equipment if it will keep you out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective but works as the verb meaning improve.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof tile is one of the overlapping pieces that shed rain off a house, protecting those inside from getting wet.

clue.text: Passenger lists fine mess aboard parts of ship

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes aboard, inside, the ship's parts

parts.note: masts are the upright spars of a sailing ship

indicators.note: used as a verb: fine is messed up, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A shipboard scene: the passenger lists are a fine mess on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is the anagram signal, not a ship's dining room, and 'aboard' puts the jumbled word inside the ship's parts after their second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's manifest is the official list of its cargo or passengers.

clue.text: Oft-repeated words from staff: "variable star"

parts.note: to man something is to staff it

indicators.note: star is variable, its letters able to change order; a variable star is also a star that changes in brightness

explanation.surface: An astronomy note from the staff about a variable star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is a verb, MAN; 'variable' rearranges STAR to TRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sound or phrase repeated in meditation, or a slogan said over and over.

clue.text: Beast galloped north and west with Shakespearean prince

indicators.note: in a down answer going north means travelling upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: galloped means ran
W is the compass abbreviation for west
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays

explanation.surface: A creature riding off north and west alongside a prince from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north and west' read as directions of travel, but one reverses and the other is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale with a long tusk, an animal and so a beast.

clue.text: Discussion venues for you and me to hold symposium's conclusion

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: you and me together are us

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter, which is the only one used

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Places where we can talk, for us to host the end of a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a place or platform for open debate, so plural forums are venues for discussion.

clue.text: Sell fifteen rare letters, reordered like this clue

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are reordered, set out in a new sequence

explanation.surface: An instruction to sell off fifteen uncommon letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has exactly fifteen letters, which is what 'fifteen' in the surface quietly confirms; 'letters, reordered' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue refers to itself, counting its own letters, so it is self-referential, describing its own nature.

clue.text: Please speak about shaking fist

indicators.note: the speaking verb goes about, around, the jumbled word

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: fist is shaken, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to talk about a fist being shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges FIST to ATISF, which SAY goes 'about'. 'Please' is a verb, not a polite word.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone is to please them or meet their wishes.

clue.text: Too much Buddhism with a shaved head — that's something many people can't tolerate nowadays

definitions.text: something many people can't tolerate nowadays

indicators.note: shaving a head removes what is on top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a glut is an oversupply
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Excess Buddhist devotion with a shaven-headed monk is more than many can stand these days.
explanation.walkthrough: The shaved head fits Buddhist monks nicely, but here it means losing the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the wheat protein that people with coeliac disease or a sensitivity avoid, and gluten-free diets are now widespread.

clue.text: Person with property consisting of narrow passageway — mostly, it's depressing

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or alley
a downer is something that brings your mood down

explanation.surface: A property owner grumbles that the cramped alley beside the house is gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A landowner is someone who holds real estate, a direct synonym for a person with property.

clue.text: Part of barrel? It's ignited again

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Asking which part of a gun barrel has been fired again.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface but the letters run straight through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Relit is the past tense of relight, meaning set burning once more, which is to ignite again.

clue.text: Arnold, e.g., turned over bread with skill

indicators.note: the two words together are turned over, read backwards
the skill word goes with the bread word, joined on after it before the pair is turned

parts.note: roti is an Indian flatbread
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Arnold, perhaps a baker, skilfully flips the bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Benedict Arnold was the American general who defected to the British in 1780. 'with' joins skill after bread, and 'turned over' reverses ROTIART.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedict Arnold's name is a byword for betrayal in the US, an example of a turncoat.

clue.text: Professor's funny bone

indicators.note: points to how a lecturing academic would say the word, so the next word is taken by its sound in speech

parts.note: funny means amusing, and that adjective is pronounced just like the bone's name

explanation.surface: An academic's elbow, the spot everyone calls the funny bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny bone' reads as one phrase but splits: the first word is the sound, the second the definition. The nickname itself is said to come from this pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, running from shoulder to elbow.

clue.text: Knitting equipment, demonstrating craft without necessity

parts.note: knitting is done with a pair of needles
craft here is cunning, and a sly person shows it

explanation.surface: Knitting gear showing off a hobby nobody really needed to take up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like handicraft, fitting the knitting, but it means guile.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlessly means in a way that was not required, an adverb matching the phrase about lacking any need.

clue.text: Chess ending with one rook and knight

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, the only one taken

parts.note: the final letter of this word
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess endgame with just one rook and a knight left on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knight' looks like another chess piece but is the definition, the title of a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title given to a knight, so a knight is addressed by it; crosswords use it for the title-holder.

clue.text: Doubtful second after the first

indicators.note: only what comes after the opening letter is kept, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a jiffy is a very short moment, a second, as in back in a jiffy

explanation.surface: Someone unsure about a runner-up finishing just behind the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second after the first' reads like a placing in a race; really it is the word for a moment with its first letter gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is an informal adjective for uncertain or questionable, a colloquial synonym of doubtful.

clue.text: Test about rising musical genre in Tombstone locale

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means going upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rock is a style of popular music

explanation.surface: Checking which kind of music was popular in the Wild West town of Tombstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tombstone, Arizona is the town of the 1881 gunfight with Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday.
explanation.definitionFit: The OK Corral is the livery stable in Tombstone, Arizona, famous as the site of the gunfight.

clue.text: Beginners in basketball exercised two hours one March

indicators.note: beginners are the starting letters of each of the following words

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Novices in basketball worked out for two hours one March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one March' looks like a date but means one of the March sisters, the four girls of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth is one of the four March sisters in Little Women, so she is an example of a March girl.

clue.text: Where lawyers meet for a drink?

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a room for members of the legal bar
surface reading: a pub where people gather to drink

explanation.walkthrough: The bar is the collective name for the legal profession, so the question mark flags a pun on a drinking room.
explanation.definitionFit: A barroom is a room where alcohol is served, and the pun suggests a room for barristers too.

clue.text: "Packaging" sounds like psychiatrist talk

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist

indicators.note: says outright that the answer is pronounced the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: rap is talk, especially frank conversation

explanation.surface: Remarking that the word for packaging is like a therapist's chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second half changes spelling: the talk word is spelt without a W, the packaging word with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink-wrap is the tight plastic film used to package goods, so it is a kind of packaging.

clue.text: Frenzied din with echo of pleasure

indicators.note: a frenzied state is wild and disordered, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild racket with echoes of delight, like a riotous party.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonic is an adjective meaning relating to enjoyment, as in hedonic psychology, so it matches the descriptive phrase.

clue.text: Dope clinches a victory over Republican pro

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed over another simply comes before it
to clinch is to grip tightly, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: dope is slang for information
taken as written
V for victory
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A doped-up athlete clinches a win against a Republican professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' looks like a professional but means supporting; IN FAVOR is the US spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pro something is to support it, so in favor matches as a predicate adjective phrase.

clue.text: Does up ridiculous phony

indicators.note: the words are put into a ridiculous, absurd order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fake person dresses themselves up in an absurd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges DOESUP; 'up' looks like a reversal signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham or not genuine, the same as fake or phony.

clue.text: Passes the Spanish fuel

parts.note: to pass away is to die
el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone hands over the Spanish fuel, as if at a filling station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' suggests handing over, but it means passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is a heavy oil burned in compression-ignition engines, a common motor fuel.

clue.text: Leader of radicals, in coalition, came together

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, which heads the answer

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
nations in a coalition are allied with one another

explanation.surface: The head of the radical faction, part of a coalition, joined forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to gather or unite for a common cause, so the past tense matches came together.

clue.text: Exaggerated motion from fluid, wild cat

parts.note: fl is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A big cat's dramatic, flowing movement in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' looks like an adjective for the motion, but it supplies its standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounce is an impatient, showy movement, such as storming out of a room with exaggerated gestures.

clue.text: On their faces, often, adult snakes exhibit slimy green spots

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so only the first letter of each word counts

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Grown snakes often show slimy green patches on their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibit' does double duty in the surface but contributes its initial to the run of first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oases are fertile, watered patches in a desert, so they are green spots in a dry landscape.

clue.text: Pests hiding in Western lair — don't worry about it

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is tucked inside it, so one piece goes within another
in an across answer going west means travelling right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
vermin are pests such as rats and mice

explanation.surface: Rats lurking in a frontier hideout, and someone saying it's nothing to fret over.
explanation.definitionFit: Never mind is an everyday reassurance telling someone not to be concerned, the same idiom as the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Filthy scum beginning to lose backward competition in sports coupe

indicators.note: the word scum is made filthy, messed up so its letters are rearranged
only the beginning, the first letter, of lose is used

parts.note: its first letter is L

indicators.note: the competition word runs backward

parts.note: a race is a competition

explanation.surface: Dirty scum starts losing a backward race in a sporty car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filthy' turns SCUM into MUSC; 'beginning to' gives L from lose; RACE run 'backward' is ECAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle car is a powerful American performance car, a two-door sporty coupe with a big engine.

clue.text: Flower reminiscent of Abner Doubleday, ultimately

parts.note: Li'l Abner was a long-running American comic strip by Al Capp, so the word recalls that name

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word, its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of this name

explanation.surface: A flower that recalls Abner Doubleday, the man once credited with inventing baseball.
explanation.walkthrough: Abner Doubleday is a red herring from baseball folklore; only the Abner calls up the comic strip title.
explanation.definitionFit: The lily is a familiar garden bloom, an everyday example of a flower.
